the lysine residue is involved in both the immunological and protein synthesis inhibitory activity of gelonin.
the positive charge of epsilon-NH _{2} group of lysine plays an important role on the ribosome inactivating property of Gelonin.
the positive charge of epsilon-amino group is essential for the immunological and protein synthesis inhibitory effects of gelonin.

the role of the positive charge of epsilon-amino group of lysine residue(s) on the ribosome inactivating property of ribosome inactivators.
the effect of modification of epsilon-NH(2) group of gelonin with 2-imino-thiolane (2IT), a bifunctional cross-linking reagent, on immunoreactivity as well as ribosome-inactivat- ing property (RIP).
the role of epsilon-NH3+ group in gelonin molecule and the results suggest that this group is important for its biological function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the modification with 2-imino thiolane (2IT) at the epsilon-NH2 of lysine residue in gelonin molecule is not only responsible for the increase in cytotoxicity of gelonin, but also for the loss of immunoreactivity.
the modification with 2-imino thiolane (2IT) at the epsilon-NH2 of lysine residues of gelonin results in loss of immunoreactivity as well as the RIP activity of the protein.
the positive charge of the lysine residues is essential for the immunological and ribosome-inactivation properties of gelonin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunoreactivity and the RIP property of gelonins are dependent on their net charge, and the charge is mainly contributed by lysine residues.

the immunological and ribosome-inhibiting properties of gelonin are not only due to the presence of the active site lysine but also to other positively charged amino acid residues present in the molecule.
the positive charge of the epsilon-NH2 residue of lysine is important for the immunoreactivity and the protein synthesis inhibiting property of gelonins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the positive charge of lysyl group is an important determinant of ribosome-inactivatory activity of gelonin and that the modification of this charge by 2-IT or other reagents may lead to the development of novel gelonin derivatives with enhanced biological activity.
